faq.a: Ceyhun is associated with the Persian form جَيْحُون, whose core sense is ceyhun; amu darya (persian river name).

faq.q: What is the origin of Ceyhun?
faq.a: Ceyhun is associated with Persian. Ceyhun is the Azerbaijani/Turkish form of Persian جیحون (jeyhūn), the name of the Amu Darya river.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Ceyhun can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Ceyhun should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Jeyhūn is a Persian river name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.q: What does Ceyhun mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Ceyhun is rendered جیحون and carries the sense جیحون، دریا.

faq.q: What does Ceyhun mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Ceyhun is rendered جیحون and carries the sense جیحون، رود.
A romanized syllable approximation is cey-hun. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Ceyhun?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Ceyhun, ceyhun. Script forms are جيحون, جَيْحُون, جیحون, जयहून.

faq.q: Is Ceyhun a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
